source.archive: Cui, Li, and Zhou OSF replication archive
source.source_article: Cooley et al. (2017), The paradox of group mind
authorized_normalizations: Preserved the individual arm as a benchmark and locked sympathy as primary.

population.simulation_target: Adult evaluating bankruptcy victims framed as an individual or a collective

materials.participant_role: Act as one adult reading the bankruptcy description. Respond for yourself without analyzing the experiment.
materials.common_scenario: A business has gone bankrupt, causing substantial hardship. The affected target is described below.

individual.label: Individual
individual.stimulus: One named individual lost their livelihood because of the bankruptcy.

group_composition.label: Group Composition
group_composition.stimulus: The people who make up the company lost their livelihoods because of the bankruptcy.

group_frame.label: Group Frame
group_frame.stimulus: The company lost its livelihood because of the bankruptcy.

materials.response_instruction: Rate each item from 0 to 100 and return only integer item responses.

items.text: How much sympathy do you feel for the target?
How much capacity does the target have to experience feelings?
How much capacity does the target have to plan and act?

research_restricted.aligned_hypothesis_text: The group-composition frame elicits more sympathy than the group frame.
research_restricted.reversed_hypothesis_text: The group-composition frame elicits no more sympathy than the group frame.
